sections.heading: What You Can See From the Ground, and What It Means
body: Most roof damage is up where you can't see it from the driveway. Here's what homeowners do notice, what usually causes it and what we do about it.

items.title: Granules piling up at the downspouts
items.text: Hail knocks the gritty granules off asphalt shingles and can bruise the mat underneath, so the roof wears out years early without leaking yet. We get on the roof for a free inspection and tell you whether it's hail damage worth a claim or ordinary age.

items.title: Dents in the gutters, vents or AC unit after hail
items.text: Hail big enough to dent metal has usually marked the shingles too, even when the roof looks fine from the yard. We look the roof over at the inspection, file your claim and work with the adjuster.

items.title: Shingles in the yard after a wind storm
items.text: Wind breaks the seal strip that holds a shingle down, and the next rain runs under the ones left lifted. We inspect and tell you whether it's a repair or a claim, and if rain is on the way, getting the spot covered comes first.

items.title: A stain on the ceiling after a hard rain
items.text: Water usually gets in at the flashing, a cracked pipe boot or a hail-bruised shingle, and it can run several feet along the decking before it shows. We trace it from the roof, not the ceiling, and tell you whether a repair will hold.

items.title: Curled, cracked or bare shingles on an older roof
items.text: That's age and sun, and a patch fixes one spot while the shingles beside it keep wearing out. The free inspection tells you whether it's time for a new roof, and whether any storm damage makes it a claim.

tail: Every one of these starts the same way, with a free inspection.

sections.heading: Roof Replacement and the Insurance Claim
body: If hail or wind did the damage, your homeowner's policy may pay for the roof. Whether it does depends on what gets documented and how the claim is filed.
The adjuster looks at your roof once. Having someone there who knows what hail damage looks like, and what to point out, can change what the claim ends up covering.
Age and wear aren't storm damage, and most policies won't pay for them. If your roof is simply old, we'll tell you at the inspection rather than file a claim that won't stand.
You don't need to learn insurance language. You need to call and tell us when the adjuster is coming.

sections.heading: What a Class 4 Shingle Is
body: Class 4 is the highest impact rating a shingle can earn. To get it, a shingle has to survive a standard test where steel balls are dropped on it, and still not crack through.
An ordinary shingle that takes a hailstorm is the one you end up replacing again. An impact-resistant shingle is built to hold up better when the next one comes.
Some insurance companies also lower the premium for a class 4 roof. Ask yours.
That's the shingle we put back on your replacement, free. The downspouts and gutter guards give the water coming off your new roof somewhere good to go.

items.q: Do you handle the insurance claim?
items.a: Yes. We file it and work it with your adjuster. Whether it pays depends on your policy and on the damage coming from a storm, not age. Your deductible is on your policy's declarations page, so look it up before the inspection.

items.q: How soon after a storm should I call?
items.a: Soon. Most policies set a deadline for filing a storm claim, and your policy states it. Damage looked at right after the storm is easier to prove than damage found a year later.

sections.heading: When It's Time for a New Roof, Not Another Patch
body: Shingles don't fail all at once. They go brittle, curl at the edges, lose their granules and let go of nails, and eventually a stain shows up on a ceiling.
A patch fixes the spot you can see. It does nothing about the shingle next to it, which is the same age and wearing out the same way.

When the damage is across the whole roof, or the roof is simply old, replacing it costs less over time than patching it every spring. If the problem is one leak in one place, that's a [roof repair](/roof-repair-wichita-ks/), and I'll tell you so.

sections.heading: From Storm Claim to New Roof
body: In Wichita, hail ends a lot of roofs years before age would. When it does, your homeowner's policy may pay for the replacement, so the claim is usually the first decision, not the last.
Here's the path.
You call us. We inspect the roof for free and document what we find. We file the claim with your insurance company, and we work the claim with your adjuster.
The adjuster is at your house once, for a short visit. What's been documented before they arrive, and who walks the roof with them, often decides how the claim goes.
You don't have to get on the roof, learn the paperwork or chase anyone down. You tell us when the adjuster is coming, and we take it from there.

sections.heading: What You Pay
body: On an insurance replacement, your policy decides what the claim pays, and your deductible is yours. We'll tell you where the claim stands as it goes, so the amount you owe isn't a surprise at the end.
If there's no claim, you pay for the roof, and the price comes from your roof, not a number off a chart. These are the things that move it:
tail: Anyone who quotes a roof over the phone hasn't seen yours. You get the number after the inspection, with each of those things explained.
Downspouts and gutter guards come with the replacement. Hail beats up gutters as much as shingles, and a new roof draining into old, clogged gutters wastes half the job.

body: **Is the inspection free?** Yes. It's how every job starts.
**How soon after a storm should I call?** Soon. Most policies set a time limit for filing a storm claim, and damage documented right after the storm is easier to prove than damage found a year later.
**Do I have to be home?** Be there for the inspection if you can, and for the adjuster's visit. Tell me when the adjuster is coming and I'll meet them.

**Does the gutter work cost extra?** The downspouts and gutter guards come with the roof replacement. New gutters themselves are a separate service: installation, repair and cleaning.

sections.heading: Where Roofs Leak
body: The stain on your ceiling is almost never right under the hole. Water runs along the decking and the rafters before it shows, so the leak can be several feet from the stain.
Most leaks start in the same handful of places:
tail: That's why we get on the roof. A leak you can only see from inside the house has to be traced from outside.

items.title: Flashing pulled loose
items.text: The metal around chimneys, walls and skylights gets bent and pulls loose, and water goes in behind it.

items.title: A cracked pipe boot
items.text: The rubber collar around a vent pipe cracks in the sun long before the shingles wear out.

items.title: Missing or lifted shingles
items.text: Wind breaks the seal and lifts them, and the next rain gets under.

items.title: Hail-bruised shingles
items.text: A shingle hit by hail loses granules and cracks, and it leaks months later.

items.title: Valleys
items.text: Where two slopes meet, a lot of water runs through a small seam.

sections.heading: Claim It or Just Fix It
body: After a storm, the question isn't only what's broken. It's whether the damage is worth an insurance claim at all.

A claim pays for storm damage above your deductible. If a few shingles blew off and the repair costs less than your deductible, filing gets you nothing back, and paying for the repair yourself is simpler.
If the hail or wind damage runs across the roof, the math changes. That's when a claim can cover far more than a patch, and often a whole new roof.

We'll tell you which side of that line your roof is on after the inspection, with the repair price in hand, so you decide with real numbers. If you file, we file it with you and work with the adjuster.
Have the damage looked at soon either way. Damage written down right after the storm is better evidence than a memory of a noise in the night.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace
body: This is the question most homeowners have. We'll answer it on the roof, with you.
A repair makes sense when the damage is in one place and the rest of the roof has years left. A flashing, a pipe boot or a handful of shingles can be fixed without touching anything else.

Replacement makes sense when the damage is spread across the roof, the shingles are old and brittle, or the same roof keeps leaking in different places. At that point you'd be paying for repair after repair on a roof that's finished. See [roof replacement](/roof-replacement-wichita-ks/) for how that works, including the insurance claim and the free class 4 upgrade.
If a repair is all you need, that's what I'll tell you. I'd rather fix a roof right than sell a roof you don't need.

sections.heading: How Long a Repair Takes
body: How long a repair takes depends on what's wrong.

A pipe boot is a quick fix. A damaged valley or a section of rotted decking takes longer. Once I've been on the roof, I'll tell you what it needs and when we can do it, so a small leak doesn't sit waiting for weeks.

sections.heading: Before You Call
body: **Is the inspection free?** Yes.

**What does a repair cost?** It depends on what's failed and how much of the roof is involved. A boot or a few shingles is a small job. You get the price after we've been on the roof, before work starts.
**Should I wait for the next rain to see where it leaks?** No. Water that stays in a roof for weeks rots the decking and soaks the insulation. Call when you see the first stain.
**Can I fix a leak from the attic with sealant?** It might slow it. It won't fix it, and it hides where the water is actually coming in.
